subject: economics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A merit good such as education is one that is:
options: Over-consumed and harmful
Non-excludable and non-rival
Under-consumed because consumers undervalue its wider benefits
Never provided by government
questions.explain: Merit goods are under-consumed because their full social benefits are undervalued by individuals.

questions.q: A key feature of a monopoly compared with a competitive market is:
options: Free and easy entry for new firms
Firms that are price takers
A single (or dominant) firm able to influence the price
Many firms selling identical goods
questions.explain: A monopoly is a single dominant seller able to act as a price maker, unlike competitive price takers.

questions.q: A rise in the price of a good, other things equal, causes:
options: An increase in demand
A shift of the supply curve
A contraction (decrease) in quantity demanded along the curve
A shift of the demand curve to the left
questions.explain: A price change causes a movement along the demand curve, not a shift; a higher price means a contraction.

questions.q: Which good is most likely to have price INELASTIC demand?
options: A particular brand of crisps
A luxury cruise holiday
One soft-drink brand among many
Petrol/fuel for most drivers
questions.explain: Necessities with few substitutes, such as fuel, tend to have inelastic demand.

questions.q: Demand for a good is described as price INELASTIC when:
options: Demand falls to zero when price rises
The good has many close substitutes
Quantity demanded changes a lot when price changes
Quantity demanded changes only a little when price changes
questions.explain: Inelastic demand means quantity demanded is relatively unresponsive to a change in price.

options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
Price is always rising
There is a shortage of the good
There is a surplus of the good
questions.explain: Equilibrium is where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied and there is no tendency to change.

questions.q: A 'public good' such as street lighting is:
options: Easily sold to individual buyers
Always provided by firms for profit
Non-excludable and non-rival, so the market under-provides it
Owned by a private monopoly
questions.explain: Public goods are non-excludable and non-rival, so markets fail to supply them and government often does.

questions.q: A fall in the cost of raw materials used by a firm will:
options: Shift the supply curve to the left
Cause a contraction in supply only
Shift the demand curve to the right
Shift the supply curve to the right
questions.explain: Lower production costs increase supply at every price, shifting the supply curve right.

options: The market allocates resources efficiently
The free market fails to allocate resources in society's best interests
Prices are always at equilibrium
There is perfect competition
questions.explain: Market failure is when free markets lead to an inefficient or undesirable allocation of resources.

questions.q: Which of these would shift the demand curve for tea to the RIGHT?
options: A fall in consumer incomes
A rise in the price of coffee, a substitute for tea
A rise in the price of tea
A rise in the price of milk, a complement
questions.explain: A dearer substitute (coffee) makes consumers switch to tea, increasing demand and shifting it right.

questions.q: A negative externality of production is:
options: A type of government subsidy
A cost imposed on third parties not involved in the transaction
A benefit to society greater than the private benefit
Always corrected by the free market
questions.explain: A negative externality is a spillover cost, such as pollution, borne by third parties.

questions.q: A demerit good, such as cigarettes, is one that:
options: Has no effect on third parties
Is over-consumed because consumers ignore its true costs
Provides benefits the market under-values
Is provided free by the government
questions.explain: Demerit goods are over-consumed because people underestimate their private and external costs.
